title: Arkret Ephemeral Broadcast Envelope
description: Wire shape for broadcast ephemeral signals — ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, ak.call.signal. These signals have wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json: they MUST NOT carry CBA reducer fields, MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root or actor_seq, MUST NOT enter reducer state, and MUST NOT be submitted via ak.events.submit. All broadcast ephemeral signals require a device_id and detached proof so receivers can verify actor source authenticity without trusting relay attribution. They are carried on dedicated ephemeral channels (sync subscribe live stream, presence/typing fanout, call signaling channel) and are dropped at TTL. Point-to-point to-device signals (ak.key.verification.*) use device-message.schema.json instead — they have a sender+recipient pair and do not match this broadcast shape. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §2.3 (wire-scope reject rule) and zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5 (ephemeral channel transport). FAIL CLOSED IN MLS-BACKED SCOPES: this envelope has only a plaintext payload branch, so in a scope whose effective encryption_profile is MLS-backed it would expose read position, typing target and the full call state machine to the Sync Service. Until the encrypted realtime surface is verified, senders, services and receivers MUST reject it there with failed_precondition / ephemeral_plaintext_in_encrypted_scope, and services MUST NOT advertise broadcast ephemeral capability for that scope. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.9.1.

kind.description: Ephemeral signal kind. MUST be one of the four broadcast ephemeral kinds; ak.key.verification.* point-to-point strands MUST use device-message.schema.json instead.

realm_id.description: Realm whose ephemeral channel carries this signal. Authorization to broadcast a signal on a Realm channel is governed by the same membership / capability rules as the corresponding durable kinds.

actor_id.description: Signaling actor. MUST be a member of the Realm (ak.member.state cell join != ban/leave/remove at receive time) for the broadcast to be admitted by other clients; receivers drop signals from non-members without surfacing them.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for all broadcast ephemeral signals; proof.verification_method fragment MUST equal this full device_id.

sent_at.description: Wall-clock send time. Diagnostic only — ephemeral signals do not participate in HLC ordering.

expires_at.description: Server / client MUST drop the signal at or after this time. Per-kind soft caps (recommended): presence ≤ 60s, typing ≤ 15s, receipt.read ≤ 30s, call.signal ≤ 30s. Signals with expires_at > sent_at + 5 minutes MUST be dropped by receivers (`invalid_param`).

payload.description: Kind-specific signal payload. Schema per kind is defined by the producing module (e.g. zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md for ak.call.signal, zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md §3.5 for ak.typing, zh/discovery/read-receipts.md for ak.receipt.read). Payload MUST NOT carry mutable governance state — that belongs in a durable event.

proof.description: Detached-JWS proof over the canonical ephemeral envelope, structurally isomorphic to the durable Event proof ($defs/event_proof in event-envelope.schema.json / models/event-and-patch.md §3). Required for every broadcast ephemeral kind (ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, ak.call.signal) so receivers can verify origin without trusting relay attribution. Signing input is the canonical proof binding object {context:'ak.ephemeral-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}; event_digest is canonical_digest of the envelope with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS). verification_method MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ak:device:<uuidv7>` id, and its controller DID MUST equal envelope actor_id. See crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5.

call_id.description: Typed call/session identifier (ak:call:<uuidv7>) scoped to the Realm. Unified with ice-config-response and media-operations so cross-channel join cross-checks key on the same form.

seq.description: Monotonic per-(realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id) sequence. Receivers MUST reject replay or rollback.

data.description: Signal-type-specific payload body (invite/answer/candidate/mute_state/...). Optional because some signals (e.g. ack) carry no body. moderation is closed by the conditional below; other signal types retain their profile-specific shape.

strand_id.description: Strand whose timeline the actor is typing into. Fanout MUST be clipped to the Strand effective scope per zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md §3.5.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key the actor is typing into. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message timelines are restricted to the discussion track, so when present this MUST be 'discussion'; when omitted receivers MUST resolve it to 'discussion'. Kept explicit so future profiles that register additional writable timelines can disambiguate typing targets without changing the envelope shape.

typing.description: true = actor started or continues typing; false = actor stopped typing and receivers SHOULD clear the indicator immediately.

ttl_ms.description: Client-side auto-clear hint in milliseconds. The envelope expires_at remains the authoritative drop deadline; per-kind soft cap for typing is 15s.

ephemeral_proof.description: Detached-JWS proof for a broadcast ephemeral envelope. Structurally isomorphic to event-envelope.schema.json #/$defs/event_proof: same kind / alg / verification_method / event_digest / created_at / jws shape, so a single EdDSA detached-JWS verifier serves both durable Event proofs and ephemeral signal proofs. The binding object carries context='ak.ephemeral-proof-v1'. The only difference is which canonical bytes feed event_digest (here: the ephemeral envelope with `proof` removed).

kind.description: detached_jws = device signature over the canonical proof binding object canonical_json({context:'ak.ephemeral-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). event_digest is the canonical ephemeral-envelope hash with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS).

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing device key. MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ak:device:<uuidv7>` id and equals envelope.device_id; verifier MUST strip the fragment for controller comparison and MUST compare that controller DID bit-identically to the envelope actor_id, then resolve the verify key from the device directory (keys/query device_signing_key, keys-operations.schema.json). Same form as event_proof.verification_method.

alg.description: Default EdDSA. Same enum as event_proof.alg for a shared verifier.

event_digest.description: canonical_digest(envelope without `proof`) per RFC 8785 JCS, isomorphic to event_proof.event_digest (which excludes proofs + unsigned).
